findings.evidence: [F1] cites only the segment definition of convexity. Proof 1.1 then uses the differentiable-convex supporting-line inequality to conclude that the auxiliary function is minimized at u, but does not derive that inequality. Add the one-sided directional-derivative argument from the segment inequality.

findings.location: Statement references; SCAFFOLD, Appendix C, Lemma 6
findings.evidence: The cited SCAFFOLD Lemma 6 (https://cs.nyu.edu/~mohri/pub/scaffold.pdf, Appendix C) assumes β-smoothness and μ-strong convexity with η≤1/β and gives a contraction factor 1−μη; it does not state convex-only nonexpansiveness for 0≤η≤2/β. Hardt, Recht, and Singer (https://arxiv.org/html/1509.01240, §3.2, Lemma 3.7(2)) gives the exact convex and smooth result. The supplier's own proof makes this citation defect nonfatal, subject to the missing inference above.

Step 3.1 invokes uniqueness for another measure ρ but cites step 2.1 as supplying its σ-finite exhaustion; step 2.1 establishes only that μ×ν is σ-finite. The rectangle formula gives ρ(X_n×Y_n)=μ(X_n)ν(Y_n)<∞ for the same covering exhaustion, which must be stated before applying uniqueness.
